# Amazon and Walmart Bring AI Agents Closer to the Purchase

By  PYMNTS   |  November 10, 2026

|

Walmart-retail-AI-digital-transformation

Walmart wants its artificial intelligence shopping agent, Sparky, to turn a handwritten holiday list into a shopping cart. Amazon wants businesses to put agents to work buying supplies and managing purchases within company spending rules. [...] The moves highlight two fronts in the companies’ competition to influence how customers buy. Walmart is making Sparky more useful for everyday shopping, while Amazon is making the case for businesses to give AI greater responsibility for purchasing. Both approaches bring agents closer to the decisions that generate transactions.

items.title: AI agents, top languages and the fastest-growing developer communities
items.summary:
GitHub set out in its Octoverse 2026 report to highlight the year's biggest developer trends around AI agents, with findings on subjects from TypeScript and Rust to Morocco and the mining industry. At first glance, the headline numbers can read like a record of what developers freely prefer. Taken together, though, much of the change appears to have causes outside developers' own taste. Those causes include the limits of the services developers depend on, the models that their tools put in [...] ## Agents now start a large share of pull requests

Illustration: Quartz

In about six months, developers handed AI agents the job of proposing new code, not just helping write it. The share of pull requests begun by agents climbed from 17% in March to over 40% by September 2026, according to GitHub. For more and more developers, the first step in a code change is now reviewing something an agent put forward instead of drafting it from scratch. [...] No single company owns this boom, and developers have more than one agent to choose from. Rival products are growing quickly alongside Microsoft's own, and OpenAI's Codex reached 4 million active users in April, up from 3 million, according to CNBC. The rise of Codex shows the shift to agents across the industry rather than inside a single vendor's product line. With several agents on offer, the strengths and limits of these tools now matter well beyond any one company. The AI a developer calls

The company said it paused certain activities and strengthened its security controls. [...] 3. Practice before an incident happens: Use the worksheet’s 15-minute tabletop exercise to walk through a hypothetical incident involving an AI agent that sends confidential information to an unauthorized recipient. Identify gaps in your response process and assign responsibility for fixing them.

turns.assistant_text:
Here is a summary of the article titled **"Reflexion: Language Agents with Verbal Reinforcement Learning"**:

- **Authors**: Noah Shinn, Federico Cassano, Edward Berman, Ashwin Gopinath, Karthik Narasimhan, Shunyu Yao
- **Abstract**: The paper introduces Reflexion, a novel framework designed to enhance the learning capabilities of language agents interacting with external environments (like games and APIs). Unlike traditional reinforcement learning methods that require extensive training and fine-tuning, Reflexion utilizes linguistic feedback for reinforcement. Agents reflect on task feedback and maintain a reflective memory to improve decision-making in future trials. The framework supports various feedback types and sources, leading to significant performance improvements across tasks, including coding and language reasoning. Notably, Reflexion achieved a 91% pass rate on the HumanEval coding benchmark, outperforming the previous state-of-the-art model, GPT-4, which had an 80% pass rate.

For more details, you can access the full paper [here](https://arxiv.org/abs/2303.11366).

However, it remains challenging for these language agents to quickly and efficiently learn from trial-and-error as traditional reinforcement learning methods require extensive training samples and expensive model fine-tuning. We propose Reflexion, a novel framework to reinforce language agents not by updating weights, but instead through linguistic feedback. Concretely, Reflexion agents verbally reflect on task feedback signals, then maintain their own reflective text in an episodic memory buffer to induce better decision-making in subsequent trials. Reflexion is flexible enough to incorporate various types (scalar values or free-form language) and sources (external or internally simulated) of feedback signals, and obtains significant improvements over a baseline agent across diverse tasks (sequential decision-making, coding, language reasoning). For example, Reflexion achieves a 91% pass@1 accuracy on the HumanEval coding benchmark, surpassing the previous state-of-the-art GPT-4 that achieves 80%. We also conduct ablation and analysis studies using different feedback signals, feedback incorporation methods, and agent types, and provide insights into how they affect performance. | | | | --- | --- | | Comments: | v4 contains a few additional experiments | | Subjects: | Artificial Intelligence (cs.AI); Computation and Language (cs.CL); Machine Learning (cs.LG) | | Cite as: | [arXiv:2303.11366](https://arxiv.org/abs/2303.11366) \[cs.AI\] | | | (or [arXiv:2303.11366v4](https://arxiv.org/abs/2303.11366v4) \[cs.AI\] for this version) | | | [https://doi.org/10.48550/arXiv.2303.11366](https://doi.org/10.48550/arXiv.2303.11366)
